subject: ACME POC — Eval methodology alignment and success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>; Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC — Recap & next steps

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about the search + summarization use case and the latency targets you mentioned (~200ms p50 for user-facing queries). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- Goal: Evaluate Redwood inference for ACME's in-app summarization and search re-ranking over a 3-week POC.
- Success criteria (initial): 1) quality: summaries rated >= 4/5 by your SMEs on our rubric; 2) latency: median <= 200ms for 90% of sampled queries; 3) cost: projected per-1M requests <$X (we'll estimate after workload sample).
- Proposed eval plan: week 0 — dataset & metrics alignment; week 1 — offline evals + grading rubric; week 2 — online shadowing; week 3 — final review & runbook.
- Ownership: ACME to provide sample queries, reference summaries, and SMEs for grading. Redwood to provision test endpoints, run offline eval scripts, and provide dashboard + per-token cost estimates.

Could you confirm the success criteria above and share: (a) a representative sample of queries (CSV), and (b) 2 SMEs who can do the rubric grading (estimate: 2–3 hours each across the POC)? Once we have that I'll upload the eval template and a first-pass grading rubric.

Attaching a quick draft of the eval plan and a blank success criteria spreadsheet for you to fill.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme-eval-plan-v1.docx, acme-success-criteria.xlsx

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC — Recap & next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming we’re aligned on scope and the 3-week timeline. A few clarifications and notes from our side: 

- Success criteria: agree with the quality + latency + cost buckets. For quality, our SMEs prefer a 1–5 scale but would like explicit guidance on what constitutes 4 vs 5 — e.g., factuality, brevity, and preservation of key entities.
- Data: I can share a CSV of ~2k representative queries by end of day Monday.
- SMEs: I’ll put you in touch with Priya Singh (product lead) and Marcus Lin (content lead) — they can each allocate ~3 hours across the POC.
- Compliance: ACME Legal asked whether Redwood will retain logs from shadowing — we need an explicit statement on retention and who can access logs. I’ve cc'd legal for visibility.

We’ll also upload a short doc with examples of expected summary length and preferred tone.

Happy to run the grading sessions live if that’s helpful, otherwise offline grading works for our SMEs.

Best,
Sara
Director, Search Product
ACME Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC — Recap & next steps

Thanks Sara — this is perfect. A few follow-ups on the eval methodology so we can lock the plan before your SMEs start grading: 

1) Offline vs online (shadow) evals:
   - Offline evals: we’ll run the provided queries against the model(s) and collect outputs into a grading spreadsheet. SMEs will grade entries blind using the rubric. This is best for broad coverage and repeatable metrics.
   - Online shadowing: we’ll mirror live traffic (read-only) through a shadow lane to measure latency in production and check for distributional drift. Shadowing gives us real latency and operational signals but requires explicit retention & access controls.

Recommendation: start with offline grading on a stratified sample of ~500 queries (we can pick stratified by query length and intent). If offline quality looks good (>= 4/5 median), proceed to a 1-week shadow window to validate latency and distribution.

2) Grading rubric (draft):
   - Factuality (0–2): 0 = incorrect/hallucinated, 1 = minor inaccuracies, 2 = factually correct
   - Relevance (0–1): 0 = off-topic, 1 = on-topic
   - Brevity/conciseness (0–1): 0 = too verbose or misses key points, 1 = concise and preserves key points
   - Tone (0–1): 0 = inconsistent with sample tone, 1 = consistent
   Total score 0–5. We map 4–5 = acceptable, 3 = borderline (requires manual review), <=2 = unacceptable.

3) Logistics & ownership:
   - Redwood provides the grading spreadsheet template and a small script for ingesting outputs and generating the blinded view for SMEs.
   - ACME to provide the sample queries CSV and assign the two SMEs (Priya, Marcus).
   - Redwood will propose two model variants (small/fast and larger/quality) for the offline pass. We’ll include per-token cost and latency estimates for both.

Next steps: I’ll send the blinded grading template and the offline eval script by EOD today. Can you confirm the 500-query sample and that Priya/Marcus are available to grade the week of July 5? Also — legal question on retention: we retain shadow logs for the POC period only (30 days) and restrict access to the engineering POC team unless you request broader access. If that works, I’ll include that in the POC runbook.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC — Recap & next steps

Quick note on operational side — thanks for the plan, Marissa. Two points: 

- Shadowing infra: we’ll provision a dedicated shadow lane in your staging region and instrument a lightweight metrics exporter (p50/p95 latency, token counts, error rates). Integrations: Prometheus + Grafana dashboard will be available.
- Data access & retention: agree with the 30-day retention for shadow logs. We’ll provide an export and a delete job at the end of the POC. If ACME Legal needs a SOC2 / data handling statement I can attach the specific excerpt from our security docs.

I’ll also include a short checklist for the engineering handoff (API keys, ingress host allowlist, sample traffic config).

—Dylan

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>, ACME Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC — Recap & next steps

Marissa / Dylan — thanks, this looks good.

Confirming: we’ll send the 2k sample CSV Monday and will extract a stratified 500-query sample for the offline grade. Priya / Marcus are available the week of July 5 to do grading (3 hours each). Shadow retention of 30 days is fine — legal will follow up only if they need the SOC2 excerpt.

I’ve attached a short doc with example summaries and tone guidance (will drop the file in the shared Drive). Looking forward to the blinded template and the offline script.

Best,
Sara

Attachments: acme-sample-summaries.pdf
